items.t: Said holding state agencies harmless keeps core services such as public safety and infrastructure fully funded.
items.q: By holding our state agencies harmless, we are ensuring that the core services our citizens rely on, from public safety to infrastructure, remain fully funded and reliable.

items.t: Said Oklahomans continue to need to protect and conserve soil, water and other natural resources.
items.q: Senate Pro Tempore Lonnie Paxton led a resolution commemorating the 90th anniversary of Black Sunday and reminded Oklahomans of the continuing need to protect and conserve our soil, water, and other natural resources.

items.t: Said the budget plan gives teachers a pay raise, adds instructional days and provides retirees a cost-of-living adjustment.
items.q: This plan provides our teachers with a much-needed pay raise to keep Oklahoma competitive, ensures our students benefit from more instructional days in the classroom and honors our commitment to retirees through a critical cost-of-living adjustment.

items.t: Said the form appointees sign pledging not to seek reelection is not enforceable as a way to remove someone from the ballot.
items.q: SB 959’s co-author, Republican Oklahoma State Sen. Lonnie Paxton, told KOSU, an Oklahoma-based NPR affiliate, that a form appointees must sign stating they won’t run for reelection is “really not enforceable from the standpoint of kicking somebody off the ballot.”

items.t: Said that without an appointment option, a U.S. Senate vacancy would have required a months-long special election and left the seat empty.
items.q: [S]o if we had a vacancy in a U.S. Senate seat, we had to go through a special election process, which would’ve taken several months for us to get through that, and that seat would be vacant the entire time, and that would’ve tipped the power of the U.S. Senate,
